_preregistration.selection: samples chosen by OFFSET only -- disjoint CORPUS chunks and fixed fractional positions in shakespeare.txt; no sample was read or picked by hand
_preregistration.rung: corpus0 must reproduce domain_gradient's text_matched cell exactly
_preregistration.primary: spread of fixed_point_fraction across prose samples vs seed noise and vs F147's prose-vs-template gap
_preregistration.secondary: the same on n_distinct_endpoints, PRE-REGISTERED (F147's endpoint arm was added after seeing the floor and was exploratory; this pays that debt)
_preregistration.why: F147's kind contrast used ONE paragraph for every model, and gemma's share of it was NINE tokens; if other prose of the same length scatters, the contrast is a single draw

verdict: RUNG (corpus0 reproduces domain_gradient's text_matched): 6 models compared, worst error 0.00e+00. Identical, so this is F147's measurement with only the prose sample varying. ANTI-VACUITY, applied SEPARATELY to the two questions. For (a): 4 of 6 models had an F147 prose-vs-template gap below 0.042 (one census start is 0.0104) -- ['Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct', 'stablelm-zephyr-3b', 'SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct', 'Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct']. Excluded: a contrast that was never larger than census noise cannot be shown robust OR fragile, and testing it either way would be vacuous. For (b): 4 of 6 models have EVERY prose sample below the floor -- ['Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct', 'stablelm-zephyr-3b', 'SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct', 'Falcon3-3B-Instruct']. Excluded there, because zero spread among floored values cannot distinguish 'stable across samples' from 'cannot move'. PRIMARY (a) -- is F147's CONTRAST robust to the draw? Per model, how close the CLOSEST prose sample comes to that model's template value: gemma-1.1-2b-it closest sample is 0.859 from template 0.000 (F147 gap 1.000) -> contrast_robust; Falcon3-3B-Instruct closest sample is 0.828 from template 0.839 (F147 gap 0.839) -> contrast_robust. Contrast robust on 2, single-draw on 0, of 2 readable. On every readable model, EVERY prose sample stays at least half the F147 gap away from the template value, so the contrast is about kind and not about which paragraph was drawn. PRIMARY (b) -- is the prose VALUE itself sample-independent? A different and stronger question, on its own gate, and it has a different answer: gemma-1.1-2b-it spread 0.141 vs seed noise 0.009 -> TEXT-DEPENDENT; Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct spread 0.057 vs seed noise 0.017 -> TEXT-DEPENDENT. Where a value is text-dependent, any claim quoting a single prose number must name its text -- even where (a) shows the contrast itself survives. DECISIVE (named before the run), gemma-1.1-2b-it carries F147's most extreme value -- prose 1.000 at its own template length of 9 tokens. Samples: corpus0=1.000, corpus1=1.000, corpus2=1.000, shak0=1.000, shak1=0.859, shak2=1.000 (spread 0.141; closest to its template value of 0.000 is 0.859). Every sample stays clear of the template value, so the perfect prose funnel is NOT a property of those nine tokens and F147's contrast survives varying the text -- across registers, not just across chunks of one paragraph. SECONDARY (PRE-REGISTERED here, unlike F147's exploratory endpoint arm -- this run is where that debt is paid), distinct greedy endpoints across the same prose samples, read for every model including the floored ones: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct [corpus0:14.5, corpus1:8.0, shak0:14.0, shak1:5.5, shak2:1.0] spread 13.5 vs seed noise 0.4; stablelm-zephyr-3b [corpus0:1.0, corpus1:9.5, corpus2:4.5, shak0:10.5, shak1:9.0, shak2:3.5] spread 9.5 vs seed noise 1.7; SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct [corpus0:4.5, corpus1:4.5, shak0:5.0, shak1:3.5, shak2:9.0] spread 5.5 vs seed noise 1.8; gemma-1.1-2b-it [corpus0:16.0, corpus1:36.5, corpus2:35.0, shak0:24.5, shak1:37.5, shak2:41.0] spread 25.0 vs seed noise 4.5; Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct [corpus0:12.0, corpus1:15.0, corpus2:12.0, shak0:6.0, shak1:45.0, shak2:4.0] spread 41.0 vs seed noise 1.7; Falcon3-3B-Instruct [corpus0:13.5, corpus1:9.5, corpus2:12.5, shak0:8.0, shak1:2.5, shak2:3.0] spread 11.0 vs seed noise 1.0. Stable across samples on 0 of 6. On the rest, which paragraph was drawn changes where the trajectories land, so endpoint claims at fixed length must name their text. BOUNDARY: 6 models, up to 3 disjoint CORPUS chunks plus 3 Shakespeare offsets, every sample selected by OFFSET and never by content, 96 starts, 2 census seeds, one length per model (its own template length). 'Prose' here is two registers, not a survey of text, and the Shakespeare stratum changes source and register together.
